sections.html:
Mount Juliet is a Nashville suburb about 17 miles east of downtown and Wilson County's largest city. Mid-2025 estimates put it at 45,172 residents, up from 39,289 in the 2020 count. Home values run high enough that a roof, an HVAC unit or a tax bill noticeably changes the check you walk away with.

Mount Juliet housing figures, 2020 to 2024 estimates
Housing measureMount Juliet
Median value, owner-occupied homes$460,100
Homes lived in by their owners72.1%
Median gross rent$2,011
Households15,960

Nearly three in four homes are lived in by their owners, so most sellers here are leaving their own house.

A Mount Juliet house gets a bill from the City of Mt. Juliet and another from the Wilson County Trustee. For the budget year that began July 1, 2026, the Board of Commissioners set the city rate at 28 cents per $100 of assessed value. After the county's latest reappraisal, the certified county rate is $1.1657 per $100.

  • Payment opens October 1, and March 1 of the next year is the delinquency date.
  • Anything paid through the final day of February carries no penalty.
  • Paying by December 31 is what secures the federal deduction for that tax year.
  • Notices go to whoever the deed shows as owner on January 1, and the city also sends data to mortgage servicers that ask.

A notice still missing at the end of October means a call to that office. The City Finance office is at 2425 North Mt. Juliet Road, 615-773-6208. The Trustee is in Room 102 of the courthouse, 615-444-0894.

Neither the city nor the Trustee can change a mailing address on the tax roll. Only the Wilson County Property Assessor can, at 228 East Main Street, Room 4, Lebanon, phone 615-444-8661. If you have moved, fix this before the sale so your last bill finds you.

On March 3, 2020, an EF3 tornado destroyed hundreds of Mount Juliet homes, along with West Wilson Middle School and Stoner Creek Elementary. Five people died across the storm's path, three of them in Mount Juliet. Local buyers remember it, and some will ask.

  • A damaged and rebuilt house should come with permits, inspection sign-offs and contractor invoices.
  • Write down the age of the roof and when it was last replaced.
  • Save insurance claim paperwork from any storm damage.

A ready folder cuts down the questions after an offer.

Building and Codes is at 115 Clemmons Road and enforces the 2018 International Codes plus the 2017 National Electrical Code for building, electrical and plumbing work. The permit counter is open weekdays from 8 to 5, and the phone is 615-773-6225. Next-day inspection requests must arrive by 2 p.m. at bldg@mtjuliet-tn.gov.

Permits cover building, enlarging, altering, repairing, moving or tearing down a structure, adding a pool, deck, arbor or storage building, and changes to electrical, gas, mechanical or plumbing systems. The department exempts fences up to 7 feet, retaining walls up to 4 feet and prefabricated pools under 24 inches deep. Ask first if you are unsure, because an open permit can delay a closing.

With two tax bills and a county recorder, small items get missed. Review these with your title company:

  • City Finance gives the city balance and the Wilson County Trustee gives the county balance for your parcel.
  • Find out whether this year's October bill has been issued.
  • Gather permit records for work since you bought, and ask Building and Codes whether any permit is still open.
  • Get a copy of your deed so the legal description matches the contract.
  • Name your mortgage servicer for the buyer's side so the payoff letter is ordered early.

Taxes are prorated between you and the buyer at closing, and the Trustee can verify what has been paid this year.

Deeds are recorded in the Wilson County courthouse in Lebanon, where the Property Assessor and the Trustee also sit. The state's transfer tax comes to 37 cents per $100 of the higher of price or value. The buyer taking title owes it, and the register collects it ahead of recording. Phone the register for current recording fees before closing.

sections.h2: Timing your sale around the tax calendar
sections.html:
Notices go out each October and the roll follows the January 1 owner, so your closing month affects who deals with which bill.

  • Close ahead of the October notice and the buyer receives the bill, though you still owe for the days you owned the house.
  • Close afterward and the bill may carry your name, so write down the split at the signing.
  • A sale in January or February leaves the prior year's bill payable without a penalty.

In any month, the title company requests balances from City Finance and the Trustee and subtracts what is unpaid from your proceeds.

sections.h2: What a sale looks like from start to finish
sections.html:
1. You describe the house, its age and any storm repairs.
  2. The buyer makes an offer and you accept in writing.
  3. The title company orders tax balances, your servicer's payoff letter and a deed search in Lebanon.
  4. Any open permit gets resolved with Building and Codes, or disclosed to the buyer.
  5. You sign. The register collects the transfer tax and records the deed.
  6. Whatever is left after the mortgage and tax balances is yours.

sections.h2: Offices and phone numbers in one place
sections.html:
Four offices cover almost everything a Mount Juliet seller needs. Save these before you list.

  • City Finance, 2425 North Mt. Juliet Road, 615-773-6208, for the city tax balance.
  • Wilson County Trustee, Room 102 of the courthouse, 615-444-0894, for the county balance and what has been paid.
  • Wilson County Property Assessor, 228 East Main Street, Room 4, Lebanon, 615-444-8661, for mailing address changes.
  • Building and Codes, 115 Clemmons Road, 615-773-6225, for permits and open inspections.

A short call to each, a week or two before you plan to sign, usually turns up any surprise while there is still time to fix it.

Buyers with a mortgage typically order an inspection and may ask for a roof or HVAC credit. Cash buyers purchase the house in its present state. Without a lender, the two of you pick the closing date, and what remains is the paperwork covered above.

It fits owners who are relocating, settling an estate or looking at repairs they would rather hand off, in a city where small items shift the numbers. Ask any buyer to put the closing date and the amount in writing before you commit, and keep copies of every payoff letter.

faqs.q: How much is the Mount Juliet city tax rate?
faqs.a: 28 cents per $100 of assessed value, set by the commissioners for the budget year starting July 1, 2026. Wilson County bills separately at its certified $1.1657 per $100.

faqs.q: What is the delinquency date for Mount Juliet taxes?
faqs.a: March 1. Payments start October 1 and stay penalty-free until February ends. A December 31 payment gets you the federal deduction for that year.

faqs.q: Where do I update my tax mailing address?
faqs.a: At the Wilson County Property Assessor, 615-444-8661, and nowhere else. The city and the Trustee cannot update the roll.

faqs.q: Is a permit required to replace a fence?
faqs.a: Not for a fence 7 feet tall or lower. Anything taller, plus electrical, plumbing or additions, needs a permit from Building and Codes at 615-773-6225.

faqs.q: How did the 2020 tornado affect Mount Juliet?
faqs.a: On March 3, 2020 an EF3 storm wrecked hundreds of homes, West Wilson Middle School and Stoner Creek Elementary. Five people died, three in Mount Juliet.
